verdict: REVISE. The empirical core ships and reproduced independently from a clean rebuild (rm -rf bin obj; dotnet build -c Release; four fresh processes, FCS 43.9.101). The measurement region of Program.fs is byte-identical to Q023's spike (diff-confirmed; only header comments + an opt-in runWarmup and a third argv branch differ), and the no-warmup control cold (my 1018ms) reproduces Q023's own run-n10.txt (1037ms) within ~2%. The first ParseAndCheckProject in Q023/Q024's OWN harness does carry the same one-time JIT/FCS-init tax Q027 found in its separate toy: warmup dropped cold by 577ms at N=10 (1018->441) and 570ms at N=300 (2365->1795) -- essentially N-independent, a cleaner 'fixed absolute size' confirmation than the executor's own 570/667. editOne/repeat raw ms barely move (measured warm), so the tax is a cold-only effect; the cold-denominated ratios rise, non-uniformly (editOneRatio N=10 ~2.7x 0.051->0.138, matching 'nearly triples'; N=300 smaller). The corrected-reading direction (editOne is a LARGER fraction of tax-corrected cold, not smaller) is right and conservative (the disclosed ~185-190ms residual tax means true cold is even lower, true ratio even higher). runWarmup was read critically and genuinely isolates a process-global tax: its own checker/DocumentSource/project never touch checkerRef/optsRef/files, so it cannot prime the measured project's per-instance cache -- it warms exactly the process-global JIT/static-init/referenced-assembly-metadata state the tax is made of. The correction lands on Q023's ratio column and its '51% of cold' prose, NOT on Q024's cost model; the pre-registration overstated the reach into Q024 (lineage's overclaim shape, mild, in the safe direction). Not KILL: numbers reproduce, isolation sound, single-sample and partial-transfer limitations disclosed.
